name: OTA Console
status: server endpoints + page implemented and live; device side (developed on another machine) already completed a real OTA round-trip against this server
description: Web console for ESP32 fleet OTA: list online/offline devices, pick a firmware release, dispatch an OTA command, and follow the command lifecycle (pending -> delivered -> success/failed). All data comes from the live API — no mock data. Dispatch is a write operation and requires a Bearer token. A device that is offline at dispatch time is refused (412): nothing is queued and nothing is delivered later — only a cancelled record is kept. Unresolved commands can be cancelled by the operator.
description_zh: ESP32 设备 OTA 云端控制台：查看在线/离线设备、选择固件版本下发 OTA 命令、跟踪命令状态（pending → delivered → success/failed），并能撤销未决命令。数据全部来自服务器实时接口，页面内无假数据；下发是写操作，需要 Bearer token。**设备不在线时下发被拒（412）**——不排队、不等上线，只留一条 cancelled 记录与页面提醒。
canonical_url_hint: Share the full base URL including the path /OTA (host is the shared firmware-server)

push_cli.what: CLI (zero dependencies, runs on the device-development machine) that publishes a build and pushes it to ONE named device, waits for the result and prints the process — the scriptable form of what this page does by hand.

list_releases.note: Existing endpoint. Page flattens projects/*/variants/*/releases/* into release options.

dispatch_command.returns: { command: { id, deviceId, type, releaseId, state, createdAt } }

errors.409: device already has an unresolved command; resend with force=true to supersede it
errors.412: device offline at dispatch time (now - lastSeen > 45s): nothing was queued and nothing will be delivered later; the server kept one cancelled record with reason=device_offline and returned it in the body. Re-dispatch once the device is back online.
errors.400: bad deviceId / bad releaseId / unsupported type

dispatch_command.note: The online check happens server-side, at the moment of enqueue (a caller that checks first would race with the device going offline/online).

cancel_command.returns: { ok: true, wasDelivered: boolean, command: Command }

errors.409: command already finished (success|failed|superseded|cancelled) — nothing to cancel

cancel_command.note: Cancelling a pending command really stops it (the device will not receive it on its next report). Cancelling a delivered command cannot stop the device (it is already writing) but DOES stop redelivery of the same command. A late result is stored in lateResult and never overwrites the cancelled state.

get_command.note: Read one command by id. Device views only expose lastCommand + unresolved, so a caller that wants to follow ONE command to its end (the push CLI does, every 2s) reads it here.

device_report.auth: device-side (no Bearer token by design — the MAC is the identity)
device_report.note: Called by the device, not by this page. Live: devices appear in GET /api/devices after their first report.

report_progress.note: Called by the device. This is what makes the OTA process visible on the page: server keeps the latest progress plus a bounded trail of phase changes (<=20). Posting progress also refreshes lastSeen, so a device blocked inside download/write is not shown as offline. Progress is a side channel — success/failure is still decided only by command_result.

command_result.note: Called by the device, not by this page. Live: it is what turns pending/delivered into success/failed with a detail string.

Device.deviceId: base MAC, lowercase hex without colons, e.g. 3485a1b2c3d4
Device.online: boolean, computed by server (now - lastSeen > 45s => offline)
Device.lastCommand: Command | null — the most recent record (may be a cancelled one)
Device.unresolved: Command | null — the pending/delivered command, if any. NOT always the same as lastCommand: an offline refusal a moment ago adds a newer cancelled record that shadows a still-queued pending command. Use this field for anything that acts on the in-flight command (the page's cancel button, the push CLI's --cancel).

Command.state: pending | delivered | success | failed | superseded | cancelled
Command.deliveryCount: number — how many times the device picked this command up (redelivery guard)
Command.deliveredAt: ISO8601 UTC | null — FIRST pickup (kept across redeliveries so the process view can show when it started)
Command.lastDeliveredAt: ISO8601 UTC | null — most recent pickup
Command.progress: { phase, percent?, bytes?, totalBytes?, message?, updatedAt } | null — latest device-reported process point
Command.trail: [{ phase, at, percent? }] — bounded (<=20) list of phase changes
Command.detail: string | null — device-reported detail, e.g. 'OTA ok, rebooted to <releaseId>'
Command.cancelledAt: ISO8601 UTC | null — set when the command was cancelled
Command.cancelReason: string | null — device_offline | cancelled_by_operator | custom operator note
Command.wasDelivered: boolean | null — true when the command had already been picked up before it was cancelled (a warning, not an error)
Command.lateResult: { state, at, detail? } | null — the device reported a result AFTER the cancellation; kept for honesty, never overwrites the cancelled state

invariants: Transport is HTTP polling (pull), not push/MQTT
deviceId is the base MAC in lowercase hex without separators
online/offline is decided by the server via lastSeen, never recomputed in the page
At most one unresolved command per device
Firmware download reuses the existing registry parts endpoint
A device that is offline at dispatch time is never queued: the command is refused (412) and only a cancelled record remains

data_source.mock: none — the page contains no built-in fake data

auth.token_storage: localStorage key fw.token — shared with the main app, never uploaded
auth.how_to_get_a_token: main app top-right key button generates a wk_ work token (needs the master token), or ask the operator

settings_link.behaviour: opening the link writes the token into localStorage (same fw.token key), strips it from the address bar, and shows a confirmation
settings_link.why_fragment: the URL fragment is never sent to the server, so the token stays out of access logs, Referer and proxies
settings_link.legacy_format: https://<host>/?settoken=<token> — still parsed for compatibility, but it is sent to the server, so prefer the fragment form
settings_link.human_use: the page has a copy-settings-link button — bookmark it once, then any browser/computer can be configured by opening the bookmark

offline_dispatch_rule.rule: a device that is not online at dispatch time is refused (HTTP 412) instead of queued: no pending command is created, nothing is delivered when the device comes back, and no wait-for-it-to-happen is implied.
offline_dispatch_rule.what_is_kept: one command record with state=cancelled and cancelReason=device_offline (bounded, rolls with the usual 20-record limit), plus a page notice. It does NOT occupy the single unresolved slot, so re-dispatching after the device returns is not blocked by 409.
offline_dispatch_rule.why_server_side: the caller would have to read the device list and then dispatch — between those two steps the device can drop or come back (TOCTOU). Only the server, at the instant of enqueue, can decide authoritatively.
offline_dispatch_rule.why_not_409: 409 already means 'a command is already unresolved'. Different situations must not share a code, or scripts cannot tell them apart.
offline_dispatch_rule.residual_window: the online decision itself lags by up to 45s. A device that drops inside that window gets its command queued as pending (it is queued, NOT waiting-for-online) and will be picked up on its next report; if it never returns, a waiting caller times out. That is the accuracy of the rule, not queueing-by-another-name.
offline_dispatch_rule.no_override: there is deliberately no --allow-offline / queue-if-offline flag: re-running the command when the device is back costs one command and avoids 'I thought I had pushed it'.

cancel_semantics.pending: really stops it — the device will not receive the command on its next report
cancel_semantics.delivered: too late to stop the device (it already took the command and is writing), but redelivery stops; if the device still reports a result it lands in lateResult and the state stays cancelled (the page labels it '撤销来晚了')

not_implemented: Nothing on the server/page side. Device-side firmware lives in another repository (see /docs/DEVICE-OTA.md) and has already performed a real OTA against this server.
Batch / fleet / broadcast dispatch ('push to every online device') — a remote flash must name one device explicitly.
watch-style auto-push, and device-initiated 'check for a newer version' (see /docs/DEVICE-OTA.md §12).
